title: Erasure case
description: The per-tenant right-to-be-forgotten evidence, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #79: the request that opened the case, the storage inventory, the sweep records, and the backup expiry windows still open. The #69 rule, moved from alerting to erasure: nothing is forgotten without a record. The Rego gate (policies/erasure) judges this case against the DEK registry: every store in the inventory needs a sweep record, an aged-out expiry window, or an explicit pending reason; backups must declare their expiry windows; sweeps must postdate the request and predate the clock; and the tenant's keys must be destroyed in the registry before the case may close. This schema mirrors the shape rules; the gate additionally enforces the cross-document rules a JSON schema cannot — the tenant must be registered with all keys destroyed, the sweep stores must be declared in the inventory, and a closed case may not still hold a pending store.

owner.description: Who owns the case and answers for its honesty. A deletion case with an owner and a review cadence is the discipline.

reviewedOn.description: Date the case was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future — a year-old sweep record says nothing about the copies made since.

tenant.description: The tenant (or subject) this case erases. Must be a tenant the DEK registry lists, with every key destroyed.

requestedOn.description: The day the erasure request arrived, YYYY-MM-DD — the day the clock started. Sweep records that predate it do not count.

requestedBy.description: The named request — a DSR id, an offboarding ticket. An erasure without a named request is deletion without cause.

status.description: The case's state. The gate fails a closed case that still holds a pending store: nothing is forgotten while a store can still produce the data.

stores.description: The storage inventory: every store where the tenant's data lives. The gate can only judge the stores the case declares — an empty inventory claims the data is nowhere, and that claim is the least believable one in the whole document.

name.description: Store name, e.g. postgres-replica-eu. Unique across the inventory; sweep records and findings cite it verbatim.

kind.description: What kind of store this is — primary, replica, vector-store, backup. The kind is what tells a sweepable store from a window-bound backup.

expiresOn.description: Required for backup stores: the day the last backup that can restore the tenant ages out, YYYY-MM-DD. A backup without its expiry window never becomes provably gone. Once passed, the expiry date is itself the record.

pendingReason.description: An explicit reason a store is not yet swept — a reindex cycle, a provider queue. A reason is a promise with words in it: it keeps the case honest and open, never closed.

sweeps.description: The sweep records: what was actually deleted, on which day, by whose hand. Nothing is forgotten without a record.

store.description: The store this sweep record covers. Must be declared in the inventory — a sweep for an undeclared store means the two documents disagree.

sweptOn.description: The day the sweep ran, YYYY-MM-DD. Must postdate the request and predate the injected clock — evidence cannot arrive before the work it evidences.

sweptBy.description: Who or what swept it — the job, the change, the hand. A record names its actor.
